html:
A reform movement among the Sanhaja Berber nomads of what is now Mauritania, begun about 1040 when the scholar Abdallah ibn Yasin came to teach strict Maliki Islam to the tribes.

His followers, called al-murabitun, men of the ribat, united the veiled tribes of the western Sahara and took the trade towns of Sijilmasa and Awdaghust. Under Yusuf ibn Tashfin they founded Marrakesh in 1070, conquered Morocco and in 1086 crossed into al-Andalus to halt the Christian advance. In the south Abu Bakr ibn Umar led the tribes until he died in 1087. They spread the Maliki school of law that still rules in North and West Africa. See also the Almoravid and Almohad empires.
sum: A reform movement among the Sanhaja Berber nomads of what is now Mauritania, begun about 1040 when the scholar Abdallah ibn Yasin came to teach strict Maliki Islam to the tribes.
